maria (prod-eng): Quick q — we saw a client using an org-scoped API key but not sending X-Project. Current gateway silently infers project from the key. Do we keep that behavior for backward compat or tighten up? Need alignment + rollout plan.

ryan (platform): Current precedence is: X-Project header -> X-Org header -> project attached to key. We added inference early to be forgiving for mobile. I think we should deprecate implicit inference but not break existing clients immediately.

olivia (sdk): SDKs can surface warnings if we add a response header. We can also ship a minor SDK that logs a deprecation message when server returns the warning header.

sahil (security): From a security POV explicit project is safer. My recommendation: 401 = invalid creds, 403 = forbidden authz, and use 409 for ambiguous inference (org key maps to multiple projects). 400 reserved for malformed requests.

maria (prod-eng): Proposal draft: 1) If X-Project present -> use it. 2) Else if key is project-scoped -> use that project. 3) Else if key is org-scoped and maps to single default project -> continue to infer but add warning header + telemetry. 4) Else if key is org-scoped and maps to multiple projects -> return 409 with actionable body. Thoughts?

ryan (platform): Sounds reasonable. I'd prefer 409 (Conflict) for ambiguous case because the request is valid but server can't choose a single target. Response should include suggestion: either provide X-Project or use a project-scoped key. Example precedence table to document:

```
Precedence (highest -> lowest):
1) X-Project header
2) project-scoped API key
3) inferred project from org-scoped key (only if single default project)
4) reject (409) if ambiguous
```

olivia (sdk): Example response body we can standardize on: 

```
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "project_required",
  "message": "Unable to infer project from org-scoped key. Provide X-Project or use a project-scoped key.",
  "hint": "https://docs.redwood.ai/auth#project-header"
}
```

And server should add header when inferring: `X-Project-Inferred: 1` and `Warning: 299 Redwood-Inference: "X-Project inference will be deprecated; see docs"`

sahil (security): Agree on headers. Telemetry event `inferred_project_used` should include `org_id` and `project_candidates_count`. If candidates_count >1 we should not infer automatically. Also rotation/narrowing of keys: if a key is rotated and becomes project-scoped mid-request, we should rely on auth evaluation at time of request.

maria (prod-eng): Rollout plan idea: 1) Add warning header + telemetry behind feature flag. 2) Canary to 5% for 48h. 3) Increase to 25% for 7d, monitor errors and SDK logs. 4) After 30d of visible warnings, flip to 409 for ambiguous cases and start returning 4xx for deprecated inference. Also add deprecation notice in docs and email big customers.

ryan (platform): I'll open a PR for gateway behavior + feature flag and docs. Will include config toggles: `auth.infer_project: enabled|warn|strict` default warn during rollout.

olivia (sdk): I'll prepare minor SDK release that watches for `Warning: "X-Project inference will be deprecated"` and logs a deprecation warning. Also add an opt-out env var `RW_SDK_ALLOW_IMPLICIT_PROJECT=true` for legacy customers.

maria (prod-eng): Good. Can we standardize the response status mapping in the docs: 
- 401 = invalid/expired key
- 403 = key valid but not authorized for that project
- 409 = ambiguous org-key needs project disambiguation
And include sample curl snippets.

deploy-bot: deploy-scheduler: Canary rollout scheduled: gateway auth-config flag `auth.infer_project=warn` -> 5% of edge nodes at 2026-04-01T06:00:00Z.

ryan (platform): :+1: I'll add tests for header precedence and for the 409 body. @olivia please link SDK PR in my gateway PR so we can coordinate release notes.

olivia (sdk): Will do. PRs incoming today.

maria (prod-eng): Thanks all — I'll add the rollout checklist to the ticket and notify customer success for outreach to high-usage org-scoped-key customers.
